title: American coconut macaroons
subtitle: chewy desiccated coconut mounds dipped in dark chocolate
excerpt: American coconut macaroons are not the delicate almond-and-meringue French macaron but something heartier: chewy mounds of desiccated coconut bound with sweetened condensed milk and egg white, baked until the outside is golden and the centre remains soft. They require almost no preparation: just fold, scoop, and bake. They are a far more straightforward biscuit than the French version sharing their name.
sourceNotes: American coconut macaroons developed separately from the European macaron/macaroon tradition. Their characteristic texture (dense, very chewy interior, slightly crisp exterior) comes from the use of condensed milk as the binding agent rather than the sugar syrup used in French macarons. The condensed-milk version became widely established in the United States through the mid-20th century and is documented in American home cookery collections of the 1950s onward.

recipe.freezeNotes: Freeze after dipping. Place on a tray in a single layer until solid, then transfer to a container.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Keep in an airtight container at room temperature for up to 5 days.

baking.bakeTemperatureNote: conventional; 16 to 18 minutes until the tips are golden and the outside has set

content.text: American coconut macaroons are held together by condensed milk, which also gives them their deep, caramel-like sweetness. The egg whites are not whipped: they are folded in unbeaten, simply to bind and add a little structure. The result is a macaroon that is dense and moist in the centre, with a golden, slightly chewy exterior. Dipping the bases in dark chocolate is optional but a very good idea.

Heat the oven to 175°C (conventional). Line two baking trays with baking paper. Combine {{desiccated-coconut}}, {{condensed-milk}}, {{egg-whites}}, {{vanilla-extract}}, and {{sea-salt-fine}} in a large bowl and fold together with a spatula until well mixed. The mixture should be sticky and hold its shape when scooped.

Scoop heaped tablespoons of the mixture onto the lined trays, spacing them 3 cm apart. Shape each into a rough mound. Bake for 16 to 18 minutes until the tips and edges are golden and the outside has set; the interior will remain soft. Rotate the trays after 10 minutes to ensure even colouring. Leave on the tray for 20 minutes before moving; they are fragile while warm.

Once completely cool, melt {{dark-chocolate}} over a bain-marie and dip the base of each macaroon to a depth of about 1 cm. Place chocolate-side up on a clean sheet of baking paper and refrigerate for 15 minutes until set.
